case_title: Deepak Gulati v. State of Haryana
evidence_type: Victim's testimony (statement under s.164 CrPC and deposition in court); medical examination and medical officer's evidence; school register (date of birth); testimony of father, hostel warden (hostile) and investigating officer; circumstantial evidence of apprehension at bus stand
mitigating_circumstances: Accused had already served more than 3 years of sentence; the Court gave him the benefit of doubt
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.365 and 376; RI 3 years and fine Rs.2,000 (s.365); RI 7 years and fine Rs.5,000 (s.376); sentences concurrent
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence affirmed
neutral_facts: The victim, a 19-year-old senior secondary student, had known the accused for some time, and he had been meeting her in front of her school. On the day in question, the accused induced her to travel with him to another town to get married, and she agreed. En route, at a lake, he had sexual intercourse with her behind bushes, which the prosecution alleged was against her wishes. He then took her to another town, where she stayed for several days at his relatives' house and was repeatedly subjected to sexual intercourse. After four days he sent her away. She stayed at a university hostel, where the warden became suspicious, questioned her, and informed her father. She later met the accused at a temple, and he persuaded her to travel with him toward a court marriage venue. At a bus stand, the victim's father and police were present and the accused was apprehended. The victim's father had lodged a complaint after his daughter did not return home. The victim was medically examined, and a school register was produced to prove her date of birth. The victim gave a statement before a magistrate and deposed in court about the events. The warden, who was declared hostile, testified about the victim's stay at the hostel. The medical officer testified that the victim had indulged in sexual intercourse and was habitual to it. The investigating officer described the search and the apprehension.
physical_harm: No injuries described; medical officer deposed the victim had indulged in sexual intercourse and was habitual to it
premeditation_planning: Not found by the Court. The Court noted a pre-decided meeting place and a plan to marry in court, but did not find premeditated criminal intent
motive: alleged: sexual gratification obtained through a false promise of marriage (the Court did not accept this)
key_evidence_accepted: Victim's own account of voluntarily leaving home and going with the accused; undisputed facts that she was 19, went willingly, and was apprehended with him at the bus stand
witness_credibility: Court noted material contradictions and improvements in witness statements, including the father's cross-examination and the victim's s.164 statement omitting the lake incident; the warden was declared hostile
post_offence_conduct: Victim made no complaint and continued to travel with the accused; the accused was apprehended at the bus stand; no evasion by the accused recorded
custody_duration: More than 3 years of sentence already served (exact custody period not stated)
bail_history: Accused on bail at the Supreme Court stage; bail bonds discharged
trial_duration: offence: 10.5.1995; trial judgment: 13.11.1998; High Court: 28.1.2010; Supreme Court: 20 May 2013
legal_representation: Appellant: Amit Pawan; State: Kamal Mohan Gupta
investigation_status: FIR registered; victim medically examined; s.164 statement recorded; investigation completed; chargesheet filed; charges framed; 13 prosecution witnesses examined
procedural_irregularity: None noted as a lapse; the Court decided the appeal on the record in the absence of the appellant's counsel
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.365 and 376 IPC and sentenced; High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction affirmed; Supreme Court: appeal allowed, conviction and sentences set aside
prosecution_argument: Not stated; the State's counsel assisted the Court in reviewing the record, and no separate arguments are recorded
defence_argument: Not stated; no appearance or arguments for the appellant are recorded
legal_principle_applied: Consent obtained on a false promise of marriage is vitiated only where the accused never intended to marry from the beginning; distinction between mere breach of promise and a false promise; s.90 IPC cannot be used to pardon the girl and fasten liability unless the accused never intended marriage; s.114-A Evidence Act not applicable
precedent_relied_upon: Uday v. State of Karnataka, AIR 2003 SC 1639; Deelip Singh @ Dilip Kumar v. State of Bihar, AIR 2005 SC 203; Yedla Srinivasa Rao v. State of A.P., (2006) 11 SCC 615; Pradeep Kumar Verma v. State of Bihar, AIR 2007 SC 3059; N. Jaladu, Re, ILR (1913) 36 Mad 453
judicial_mitigating_factors: Accused had already served more than 3 years of sentence; benefit of doubt given
